title: FIAP®-Digital in Autism: A Roadmap from Construct Validation to Human-Supervised, Equity-Aware AI-Assisted Translational Stratiﬁcation and Precision Care
content: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by substantial heterogeneity in biological burden, adaptive reserve, developmental timing, therapeutic engagement, neuroplastic accessibility, and response to intervention. This heterogeneity is not a single problem. It includes population-level diversity across sex, age, ancestry, ethnicity, language, culture, service access, and socioeconomic context, as well as individual neurobiological heterogeneity that cannot be reduced to group-level averages. This dual structure creates a major translational challenge for precision-oriented autism care: individualized stratification must be biologically and developmentally meaningful while also being equitable, calibrated, and generalizable across diverse populations.This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes FIAP®-Digital as a long-term, human-supervised, AI-assisted roadmap for integrating candidate constructs within the Framework for Integrated Autism Precision Care (FIAP®). The framework is organized around proposed constructs, including the Biological Burden Index (BBI), energetic capacity, adaptive neurodevelopmental window accessibility, therapeutic engagement accessibility, and neuroplastic capacity. These constructs are not presented as validated clinical metrics. Rather, they are hypothesis-generating translational constructs requiring staged operationalization, reliability testing, construct validation, predictive validation, fairness assessment, and prospective clinical utility evaluation.The revised roadmap specifies a layered computational architecture: multimodal data inputs, data provenance and quality control, construct-level estimation, uncertainty estimation, translational profile inference, clinician-guided interpretation, longitudinal updating, and equity-aware governance. It also distinguishes FIAP®-Digital from existing frameworks such as RDoC, SPARK, and broad biomarker-discovery approaches. FIAP®-Digital is not intended to diagnose autism or automate treatment selection. Its proposed contribution is to organize the conditions under which therapeutic input may become more or less accessible for a specific autistic individual at a specific time and in a specific context.We propose falsifiable hypotheses and validation criteria for evaluating whether FIAP®-Digital adds incremental explanatory or predictive value beyond existing indicators such as age, adaptive functioning, symptom measures, intervention intensity, sleep, fatigue, and clinician ratings. We also define equity-aware validation requirements, including population-stratified profile discovery, subgroup calibration, intersectional error analysis, missingness auditing, and monitoring of longitudinal drift. FIAP®-Digital should remain a research roadmap until its constructs, profiles, algorithms, fairness safeguards, and clinical utility are empirically demonstrated.
